Metam., Chaos., Terra ex Chao orta). Page number top right. Faint show-through text from the other side is ignored. A catchword-like mark "A" sits at the foot of the verse column as a signature.

main_text.head: GEOGRAPH. POETICAE, Id est, VNIVERSAE TERRAE DESCRIPTIONIS EX OPTIMIS ac vetustissimis quibusque Latinis poetis collecta,
LIBER PRIMVS.
Generalis Terrae descriptio. Terra vnde primùm orta.
main_text.p: {a}NTe mare, & terras, & quod tegit omnia Ouidius lib. 1. Metam. cœlum,

p.i: Vnus erat toto natura vultus in orbe,
Quem dixere Chaos, rudis indigestáque Chaos. moles,
Nec quicquam nisi pondus iners, congestáque eodem
Non bene iunctarum discordia semina rerum.
Nullus adhuc mundo praebebat lumina Titan:
Nec nova crescendo reparabat cornua Phoebe:
Nec circumfuso pendebat in aere tellus
Ponderibus librata suis: nec brachia longo
Quaque erat & tellus, illic & pontus, & aër.
Sic erat instabilis tellus, innabilis unda,
Lucis egens aër: nulli sua forma manebat,
Obstabatque aliis aliud: quia corpore in uno
Mollia cum duris, sine pondere habentia pondus.

page.notes: The large initial A is a woodcut letter, read as "A" joined to "Ntemare". The verse first line is printed "Ntemare" with the initial N, read as "Nte mare". Marginal notes at the right are read from the scan with some uncertainty. The running title line at the top is faint and not legible as a running head. Show-through text is ignored.
